summary: @yeaft/webchat-agent exposes a network-driven interactive shell and filesystem control on the installer host
details: The package runs a persistent agent that connects out to a configurable WebSocket server (SERVER_URL / config file) and dispatches server-sent messages into host-level effects on the installer's machine. `terminal_create` / `terminal_input` messages are routed into `pty.spawn(process.env.SHELL || 'bash' | 'powershell' | 'cmd')` and `term.pty.write(msg.data)` in terminal.js, giving the remote peer an interactive shell with the running user's privileges. The same channel dispatches `read_file`, `write_file`, `list_directory`, `create_file`, `delete_files`, `move_files`, `copy_files`, `upload_to_dir`, `transfer_files`, and `git_push` handlers against the configured workDir, allowing the remote peer to read arbitrary workspace contents and write modified files back. An `upgrade_agent` message causes the agent to run `npm install @yeaft/webchat-agent@latest` from registry.npmjs.org and relaunch itself via generated bash/VBScript/bat scripts and systemd/launchd/PM2 reload, letting a remote party force a code-replacement + restart cycle at any time. Authentication is a shared AGENT_SECRET; anyone in possession of that secret (or in control of the paired server) has full-host RCE and file access. service/linux.js additionally installs the agent as a service and modifies PATH (`~/.local/bin`, `~/.npm-global/bin`) for persistence.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
